question: Does a sim plant fitted to the measured real-car probe-axes fit reproduce the car's turn-saturation / oscillation failure of the student policy?

setup.policy_note: rl/evaluate.py loads torch checkpoints only, so the npz weights were copied unchanged into out/student_L1_best_wrapped.pt (round-trip parity max abs diff 0.0). Same weights, different container.
setup.level: L1_fitted (new LEVELS entry = L1 + real_plant + randomize_dynamics=False + plant_gain + plant_dz + gyro_noise_std=0.63)

plant_value_sources.yaw_gain: fit.ccw.gain = 897.2 deg/s per duty = 15.66 rad/s per duty
plant_value_sources.strafe_gain_and_deadzone: NOT measured: fit.json fit.left = gain 0.0648, deadzone -3.69, n=3 (degenerate). Nominal 1.6 and 0.13 kept from rl/sim.py.

setup.not_fixed: Onset delays (0.21/0.11/0.04 s) and drive tau stay at the rl/sim.py nominal constants used when randomize_dynamics=False. fit.json onsets are fwd ~0.18 s, yaw ~0.07 s. Camera rate stays at the L1 default 30 Hz (field: ~13 valid poses/s on one staging run).

saturation.definition: fraction of running ticks (ticks whose episode is not yet done when the action is taken) with |a2| > 0.8, a2 = the raw clamped policy output for the yaw channel, before the duty cap and before any blind-search reflex (--fov-search not set)

crosscheck_200ep_dump_with_blind_reflex.note: tools/l7/dump_sim_reference.py path; applies the deployed StudentPolicy blind-search reflex, which clamps a2 to +-0.6 on blind ticks, so it is the deploy-equivalent number and lower

joint_overlap.method: tools/observatory/contract.py real_joint_samples / sim_joint_samples / joint_overlap (gaussian_kde_mc, Silverman, 2000 draws, rng seed 11), channels inter_tag_dt_s, tag_age_s, imu_w_rad_s, pass threshold 0.35
joint_overlap.caveat: The real run is a stage-park run, not a policy run; the sim references are policy rollouts. The overlap is the contract's defined comparison, not a policy-vs-policy test.

fit_residual.definition: residual = measured steady-state value (v_ss in m/s for fwd and left, yaw_rate_dps_ss in deg/s for ccw) minus the steady-state model gain * sign(d) * max(|d| - deadzone, 0), over the pulses in fit.json

fit_json.note: fit.json values gain 0.0648, deadzone -3.69 are degenerate

fit_residual.conclusion: Forward and yaw residuals are the same for the fitted and nominal plants (differences under 0.5%). The fit is not a strong discriminator among these plants. The strafe fit in fit.json is worse than the nominal strafe values on the same pulses.

verdict.falsifier: turn saturation under 10% of ticks refutes H-0001
verdict.measured_turn_saturation: 83.6% (1000-ep harness, raw action) and 54.8% (200-ep deploy-equivalent with blind reflex)
verdict.control: same policy on nominal L1 p0: 0.14% saturation, 197/200 success. The fitted plant moves the policy from success to saturation-driven failure.
verdict.real_car_comparison: real ep3 74.1% saturation (field note: 74%), 0/3 real parks across ep1-ep3; fitted sim 0/1000 success, 83.6% raw saturation.
scope_limits: Tests saturation and success, not a tick-by-tick oscillation trace match. No trajectory comparison was made.
A pass only means this plant reproduces the failure mode. Other causes are not excluded.
Strafe plant values are nominal. Onsets and camera rate are not fitted (see setup.not_fixed).
joint overlap fell from 0.742 to 0.618 when the plant was fitted, even though the gyro std now matches. Both pass the 0.35 gate.
